item.description:
Terminal view on your other devices now shows what the terminal shows. A phone, iPad or second Mac that was watching a terminal was being sent the program's output with its screen-control codes removed, so every repaint piled up as typed text. It now gets the real output, a fresh picture whenever the size changes, and the right rows for a plain shell. Taking a terminal with Use Here no longer makes the program repaint twice.
Séance is much quieter. With many chats working it could use most of a processor core just keeping the sidebar and window up to date; that is now a few percent, and resizing the window stays smooth.
Long messages no longer go missing. When Séance's helper typed a message for you (a chat with no window on this Mac, or Séance closed), anything over about 4,000 characters was lost while your phone showed it as sent.
⌘⇧[ and ⌘⇧] switch to the previous and next tab.
The helper no longer goes down when a device's connection is dropped at the wrong moment, and it reads a long conversation once instead of again on every refresh. The usage widget reloads far less often.
Chats on a computer with no Séance window (Linux, or a Windows PC through WSL2) now show their terminal correctly on your devices, and that computer reopens its chats by itself after it restarts.
